title: Can zero reward raise an estimate?
hook: A transition gives no reward. What can the next state change?

knows: A grid world: an agent moves, collects points, ends at a goal.
doesNotKnow: Explain why a zero-reward experience tuple can increase an action-value estimate.

objective: Explain why a zero-reward experience tuple can increase an action-value estimate.
misconception: The immediate reward is the whole update.

claims.text: Start/right reward0 leads to Bridge with Q(left)=2 and Q(right)=4. The separate terminal tuple uses old1 and reward4; a stored terminal99 is ignored.
claims.source: src/demos/ai/ai-q-learning/Demo.tsx#picture#tuple; src/demos/ai/ai-q-learning/model.ts + model.test.mjs finite author implementation reproduction; https://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/~dayan/papers/cjch.pdf — Watkins and Dayan (1992), §2, pp280–281; experience update and maximum next estimate; body opened 2026-10-19.

claims.text: With α=.5 and γ=.5, old0 gives target2/new1; replay old1 gives target2/new1.5. Terminal continuation0 gives target4/new2.5.
claims.source: src/demos/ai/ai-q-learning/Demo.tsx#picture#trace; src/demos/ai/ai-q-learning/model.ts + model.test.mjs finite author implementation reproduction; https://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/~dayan/papers/cjch.pdf — Watkins and Dayan (1992), §2, pp280–281; experience update and maximum next estimate; body opened 2026-10-19.

claims.text: With γ=0, zero-reward Start updates remain0. Primary values 0→2→1, 1→2→1.5 and terminal1→4→2.5 are retained.
claims.source: src/demos/ai/ai-q-learning/Demo.tsx#summary#contrast; src/demos/ai/ai-q-learning/model.ts + model.test.mjs finite author implementation reproduction; https://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/~dayan/papers/cjch.pdf — Watkins and Dayan (1992), §2, pp280–281; experience update and maximum next estimate; body opened 2026-10-19.

claims.text: γ discounts the next estimate; α sets the fraction moved toward the target. Fixed experience replay demonstrates the update, not convergence.

recall.question: Old2, reward1, next values2/6, γ=.5, α=.5. What is the new estimate?
recall.why: The target is 1+.5×6=4; halfway from 2 gives 3.
